facts.statement: The type specimen was originally assigned to the genus Styptobasis and discovered by Edward Drinker Cope in the Illinois Basin black coal shales.
facts.quote: The type specimen, assigned to the genus Styptobasis, was discovered by Edward Drinker Cope in Illinois Basin black coal shales.

facts.statement: Rainer Zangerl reassigned the species S. aculeata to the genus Cobelodus in 1973.
facts.quote: Rainer Zangerl reassigned S. aculeata in 1973 to the genus Cobelodus

facts.statement: Cobelodus was a predator that grew up to 1.5 to 2 meters long.
facts.quote: Cobelodus was an up to 1.5-2 m long predator.

facts.statement: Cobelodus had unusual 30 cm long, flexible cartilaginous tentacles sprouting from its pectoral fins.
facts.quote: Another unusual physical feature of Cobelodus are the 30 cm long, flexible cartilagenous 'tentacles' sprouting from its pectoral fins.

facts.statement: The purpose of the tentacles on Cobelodus is unknown.
Cobelodus lived from the late Carboniferous to the early Permian period.
facts.quote: Cobelodus is an extinct genus of cartilaginous fish known from the late Carboniferous to the early Permian period.

facts.statement: Cobelodus fed on mollusks, octopuses, and crustaceans.
facts.quote: Se alimentaba de moluscos, pulpos y crustáceos.

facts.statement: Cobelodus is classified in the extinct order Symmoriida.
The parent group of Cobelodus is the family Symmoriidae.
Cobelodus lived between the Visean and Artinskian stages, from 335.4 to 283.3 million years ago.
facts.quote: Time range: Visean to Artinskian (335.4 to 283.3 million years ago)

rejected.statement: Cobelodus possessed a bulbous head, large eyes, a high-arched back, and a dorsal fin positioned far to the rear above the pelvic fins.
rejected.quote: It had a bulbous head, large eyes, a high-arched back, and a dorsal fin placed far to the rear, above the pelvic fins.
